sentences.text:
Bishnu Majumder @ Tapan & Ors vs Unknown on 23 March,
2023

Author: Bibek Chaudhuri
Bench: Bibek Chaudhuri
23.03.2023 Srimanta Crr/1033/2023 In the matter of : Bishnu Majumder @ Tapan & Ors.
Mr. Rajdeep Mazumder, Mr. Moyukh Mukherjee, Ms. Aishwarya Bazaz ...for the petitioners.

The petitioners have challenged a criminal proceeding being Gaighata Police Station Case No.
254/2023 dated 15 th March, 2023 under Sections 420/448/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code with a prayer to quash the said proceeding on the ground that the Trial Court wrongly directed the Officer-in- Charge of Gaighata Police Station to treat an application under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed on 14th March, 2023 against the petitioners.

In order to appreciate the crux of the problem the following facts are required to be recorded:-
One Pramatha Ranjan Thakur established All India Matua Mahasangha, a religious organization of the believers of Matua faith.
After the death of Pramatha Ranjan Thakur, his widow, Binapani Thakur became the sanghadhipati.
In the wedlock between Pramatha Ranjan and Binapani three sons were born, namely Kapil Krishna Thakur, since deceased, Mridul Krishna Thakur, since deceased, and Manjul Krishna Thakur.
The de facto complainant, Mamata Bala Thakur is the second wife of Kapil Krishna Thakur, since deceased.
After the demise of Binapani Thakur, Mamata Bala Thakur claimed herself to be the Sanghadhipati on the basis of a deed of gift or arpannama executed by Binapaani in the year 2015.
The said deed of gift was challenged by filing two suits - one by Manjul Krishna Thakur and another by some members of Matua community along with the sons of Manjul Krishna.
Both the suits are pending in the competent Civil Court.

It is the grievance of Mamata Bala Thakur, claiming to be the sanghadhipati that as sanghadhipati she is responsible to conduct an yearly fair and festival of All India Matua Sangha from 18th March, 2023 to 24th March, 2023.
On 14th March, 2023 he noticed that some persons have exhibited posters and festoons for allotment of space in the fair ground to erect stalls.

It is alleged by the complainant that as sanghadhipati the complainant and the official committee of Matua Mahasangha are empowered to allot plots or spaces for setting up stalls during the fair and festivals.
However, the petitioner nos. 1 and 2 collected approximately Rs.21,00,000/- by giving false promise to innocent persons for setting up stalls in the fair ground.

It is submitted by the complainant that previously she informed the matter to the Officer-in-Charge of Gaighata Police Station and the Superintendent of Police,

sentences.text: Therefore, she approached the Court by filing an application under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure with the above allegation.
It is learnt from the submission made by Mr. Mazumder that there remains a dispute as to who will be the Sanghadhipati of All India Matua Mahasangha.
It is alleged by the third son and grandson of Binapani Thakur that the third son of Binapani ought to be the Sanghadhipati because of the fact that he is now the living descendant of Binapani.
It is also submitted by Mr. Mazumder that in general body meeting of All India Matua Mahasangha, Santanu Thakur, the second son of Manjul Krishna Thakur elected as the Sanghadhipati.
Mamata Bala Thakur being the second wife of Kapil Krishna Thakur, since deceased was not accepted by the general body of All India Matua Mahasangha to be its Sanghadhipati.

Be that as it may, it is rightly pointed out by Mr. Rajdeep Majumder, learned Advocate for the petitioner that the opposite party no. 2 made a false affidavit stating that before filing application under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
she made the similar complaint to the Officer-in-Charge of Gaighata Police Station and the Superintendent of Police.
However, no such complaint has been filed.

Mamata Bala claimed the letters of Police assistance submitted by her before conducting the fair and festival as the complaint submitted before the Officer-in- Charge and the Superintendent of Police.
However, these are not the complaints.
I am in agreement with Mr. Mazumder that Sections 154(1) and 154(3) was not complied with before filing the application under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
In view of such circumstances, the instant revision is admitted.
The Investigating Officer of the case is directed not to proceed with the investigation until further order.

The petitioners are directed to serve copy of the instant revision to the opposite party no. 2 under registered speed post with acknowledgement due and file affidavit-of-service within three weeks from the date of this order.
The State of West Bengal be served through the learned Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta.
The instant revision is made returnable after six weeks.
In the meantime, Lower Court Records be called for.
( Bibek Chaudhuri, J. )
